newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Qingling Motors says H1 sales up.
newsitem.headline: China's Qingling Motors says H1 sales up.

text.p: China's Qingling Motors Co Ltd saw its first-half sales increase year-on-year and is set to reach sales targets for 1997 with an expected boost from the launch of a new truck, a company official said on Thursday.
The light truck maker had sold more vehicles in the first six months of this year than the 16,600 it sold in the same period last year, said company secretary Qian Sheng.
Qian did not give the company's sales revenue in the first half.
The company, based in Chongqing in the southwestern province of Sichuan, hoped to sell between 36,000 and 38,000 vehicles for all of 1997, more than the 34,400 it sold last year, Qian said.
"We can reach the target," Qian told reporters in Beijing.
Qingling would launch a new line of pick-up trucks in late 1997 and hoped to sell between 5,000 and 6,000 of the vehicles by the end of the year, he said.
Analysts have said Qingling, which has a cooperative deal with Isuzu Motors Ltd to use the Japanese firm's name and technology, has captured about 21 percent of China's top-end light truck market.
